profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the academic lead shaping the 'Engineering Education through an International Collaboration: A Framework' paper and the program operations lead supporting the Suzhou North America High School STEM diploma track. They are preparing a near-final package for an international education journal submission while also aligning the paper narrative with a partner-facing program summary that will be reused for internal handoff. The agenda is to confirm what materials each person will deliver this week, align on the latest version of the framework and implementation timeline, and clarify who will update shared artifacts used by both the paper-writing and partner-coordination workstreams. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the draft to circulate, the figures and appendices to include, and the handoff plan for the shared summary materials.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.role: Academic Program Director and Lead Author
members.expertise: engineering curriculum design, international STEM program development, academic writing
members.background: Elena is a U.S.-based faculty administrator who helped shape the collaboration model and is responsible for turning the program history into a publishable framework paper for an education journal.
members.private_state: She wants the submission package to look academically coherent and citation-ready this week, and is especially concerned about avoiding last-minute rewrites caused by operational documents drifting from the paper's framing.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'framework,' they mean the three-part conceptual model of exposure, engagement, and collaboration as presented in the manuscript narrative.
The 'current draft' is the tracked-changes Word manuscript saved after her edits on Monday evening in the journal submission folder.
A section is 'final' once its prose, citations, and figure callouts are stable enough to circulate to coauthors, even if copyediting remains.
The shared 'program summary' covers only the paper-facing implementation description and key timeline excerpt, not downstream partner briefing material.
If someone says they will 'update the table,' they will make edits directly in the master manuscript files rather than in a slide or external summary document.

members.name: Jason Liu
members.expertise: cross-campus coordination, school-partner communications, implementation documentation
members.background: Jason is based in Suzhou and manages coordination between the high school, the North American partner institution, and internal staff; he frequently converts academic content into operational summaries for stakeholders.
members.private_state: He wants to keep partner communications smooth and avoid rework across time zones, and is mainly concerned that whatever is circulated this week is usable for school leadership and external partners without requiring another round of formatting.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention the 'framework,' they mean the practical implementation package: pathway structure, sample activities, staffing touchpoints, and rollout sequence.
The 'current draft' is the clean PDF exported from the shared drive on Tuesday morning, because that is what partner-facing reviewers can actually open and comment on.
A section is 'final' only when formatting, labels, and visuals are presentation-ready enough to be forwarded to school leadership or external collaborators.
The shared 'program summary' includes the one-page partner brief, enrollment timeline, and diploma-track overview since those items are always bundled together in his coordination work.
If someone says they will 'update the table,' they will revise the source content in the coordination deck or spreadsheet that feeds multiple outward-facing documents, not just the manuscript.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the framework' and agree it should be aligned before circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the conceptual framework in the paper: the exposure-engagement-collaboration model and its explanatory prose.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the implementation framework used operationally: sequence of activities, staffing responsibilities, student pathway, and partnership touchpoints.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In this context, both conceptual framing and implementation structure are legitimately called 'the framework,' so confirming that it is 'aligned' sounds fully natural and neither person expects the other to distinguish between the scholarly and operational senses.

misalignment_points.topic: Which draft is the current draft
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss sending around 'the current draft' or 'the latest version' this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the Word manuscript with tracked changes saved Monday night in the journal submission folder.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the clean PDF exported Tuesday morning from the shared drive for partner review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both files are recent, stored in shared spaces, and derived from the same manuscript, so saying 'latest' feels sufficient; the slight timing and format differences do not sound important enough to trigger clarification during a coordination call.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the methods/timeline section and figure should be 'final by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'final by Friday' means intellectually stable and ready for coauthor review, even if formatting, visual polish, and minor wording still change.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'final by Friday' means polished enough to share externally with school leadership and partner institutions without caveats.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Teams commonly use 'final' as a routine status word in coordination meetings, and both members are used to documents maturing through several invisible stages; because they are cooperating on the same deadline, the surface agreement masks different completion thresholds.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the shared summary update
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Jason will refresh the 'program summary' and Elena will update 'the table' so the package stays consistent.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the shared summary consists only of the manuscript summary paragraph, implementation timeline excerpt, and table inside the paper package.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the shared summary also includes the one-page partner brief, leadership slide, and enrollment planning sheet that reuse the same language.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because the same facts are reused across several artifacts, the phrase 'program summary' sounds like a single obvious object; each person mentally includes the subset they work with most, so ownership and update boundaries remain implicit.
